items.title: Clarence Ford Interview, 1975-12-10
items.q: But my Uncle Manny started me out.

ctx.x: Hospital? Yes. And we were talking about the musicians in your family before we ever had

the machine on. Well, far back as I know, my grandfather was a cornet player, Martin Gabriel. I was a drummer. And his sons, they all played, I believe. Martin Gabriel, I could call him Manny, my Uncle Manny. Uncle Clarence plays piano. Uncle Manny plays saxophone clarinet. He was a drummer with Louis Armstrong before he left New Orleans. And my Uncle August Lundwa, he married mine. He played bass. I know you know him. Uncle Clarence plays bass. And I was there, I have cousins. My Uncle had six boys and they all…
Yeah, I heard, I think, that, uh, a lot of people played across the river.

items.title: Manny Gabriel Interview, 1965-07-27
items.q: Before he went to war, I had a big band and I had my little nephew, Clowns Ford.

ctx.x: Well I was going to ask you. Go ahead.

Later on it got to the point, I didn't help all them fellas on the trumpet I got out the band with. I couldn't get no trumpet players at all. They stick with me. Right up. So anyhow, what I did, I take in and... So I said I'm going to break my boys in on the trumpet. And I know they got to play with me whether they want or not. Because I'm the daddy. So I take in Morton and August. And I learned down the trumpet, how to play the trumpet. And I learned trumpet from old man Delmore. And August and Mauret, I often…
